summary: The query formats every required row once and performs the mandated descending ordering, matching the unavoidable output and comparison-ordering work with no genuine slower principal query class to calibrate.

optimality.argument: Without assuming a favorable physical or index order, a correct result must inspect and emit all r rows and arrange arbitrary distinct person_id values in descending order; comparison ordering has an Omega(r log r) lower bound, while one projection followed by ORDER BY achieves O(r log r).

replacement_checks.evidence: The output contains every input row and requires a total descending order over arbitrary distinct primary-key values.
The query performs constant-size formatting per row and one descending ORDER BY over person_id.
Regression fixtures cover all profession initials, shuffled identifiers, a single row, names containing spaces, formatting punctuation, and descending order.
